reasoning_traces.think:
Offensive line snap counts are fundamental sovereign primitives because they directly measure the health and continuity of the most structurally critical unit on the field. The core principle that starting QBs and five offensive linemen play nearly 100% of snaps when healthy creates a natural null hypothesis. Any deviation from this norm—especially mid-game drops below 95%—immediately signals injury, coaching intervention, or tactical substitution. This deviation is the strongest real-time edge indicator in prop betting because it bypasses traditional injury reports and becomes empirical evidence. Tight ends exhibit personnel-dependent performance scaling: those limited to 11-personnel rely on raw volume (catches, targets) while those restricted to 12-personnel must demonstrate elite efficiency despite reduced opportunities, creating a predictable floor ceiling. For running backs, the bell cow-committee dichotomy maps cleanly to statistical regimes: true bell cows (>300 half-PPR points) represent high-conviction investments with low variance, whereas committees introduce strategic uncertainty that can be quantified through timeshare analysis. These four primitives form a unified mathematical architecture: they describe static roster roles (OL, TE personnel), dynamic injury signaling (midgame deviation), and stochastic timeshare structures (RB classification). They are sovereign because they derive from immutable rules of football operations rather than derived statistics.
